notes.title: VSync
notes.notes: You should find any issues caused by VSync on screens with a refresh rate above 60hz have been resolved. PC accidentally got caught up in some preparations I was making for Switch 2 in recent weeks!

notes.title: Extremely Soft
notes.notes: [p]- Slight adjustments to the layout of options.[/p][p]- Being challenged to raise the difficulty is rarer, only happens below "Very Hard", and the consequences of saying no are lower (-1% instead of -5%).[/p][p]- Showing the map between scenes when roaming is now optional (but remains recommended for specs that aren't powerful enough to load instantly!). This means you can now seamlessly walk through the curtain.[/p][p]- New female flesh at #16-18 and new male flesh at #22-23.[/p][p]- New head shave at #18.[/p][p]- Costumes only change in real-time if they are different.[/p][p]- Eliminated team-mates in "War" matches do not cause your character to change (and when you are eliminated you get to control somebody else on a slight delay instead of instantly).[/p][p]- Confrontations can no longer end from exhausting yourself after your own move.[/p][p]- Cannot catch objects while handcuffed.[/p][p]- Adapted the timing of floods for 60fps.[/p][p]- Being underwater when roaming makes you 25% colder.[/p][p]- Shivering animations don't carry over to menu screens.[/p][p]- Victims of assault mention nearby allies.[/p][p]- Improved delivery of a rare betrayal storyline.[/p][p]- Improved AI is better at finding alternate routes.[/p][p]- More efficient texturing of the plane interior.[/p][p]- Slightly improved sound quality on Themes 52-54.[/p][p]- Ironically, the game console prop is available on every platform except Switch.[/p]

notes.title: All Gas, No Brakes
notes.notes:
- Even more characters can be used in matches (remember to make it inter-promotional to go beyond the limits of one roster!) and a new "Extended" FX option takes longer to remove splatters or eliminated opponents.
- Characters are added/removed as quickly as you can tap the button - whereas holding it now takes you to a screen where you can hand-pick ALL participants by name! This function can be accessed instantly with a middle mouse click, where right clicks also now instantly remove a specific character.
- Choosing not to participate in a match now changes the "Play" tab to "Watch".
- Character outlines when switching controls in multiplayer are now optional.
- More assertive AI is better at judging ranges (especially with weapons), and a new "Extremely Hard" setting makes it even more difficult to defeat CPU opponents!
- Continued success at a lower difficulty level in career mode may challenge you to raise it.
- More intuitive target selection is more interested in those nearby (in the direction you hold) instead of randomly browsing through every single character.
- Fixed an issue that may have caused extra controllers to not have their meters displayed.
- New taunts include: "Point At Sky", "Statuesque", "Rewind", "Loaded Fist", and a handful of new "Remove..." taunts can actually change your costume in real-time!
- New Middle Eastern headwear at #46 (rest in peace Sabu).
- New female singlets at flesh #14-15.
- New falling animations include slumping forwards or backwards against a wall.
- Swinging weapons can become entangled (relative to the "Skill" and timing of the defender).
- Many strike counters (and entanglements like double clotheslines) are less common as standard, especially without human input (i.e. an abandoned controller will never fight back).
- Powerful strikes & crushes are powerful enough to end a match on an "Adrenaline" rush (but use up more of it).
- It's less likely to counter finishers but not impossible.
- Spamming the same move makes it twice as likely to fail.
- Holds that have very few counters are easier to break the standard way.
- Alternate left-handed slap and lower slaps with either hand.
- People with no arms favour kicks, etc.
- Having no arms makes it harder (but not impossible) to get back up to your feet.
- Missing arm limbs increase the chances of falling while climbing.
- Weak strikes stop springboards as much as a strong strike.
- Needing the toilet distracts you from attacking/grappling.
- Improved logic when stripping costumes to remain tattooed, etc.
- More relevant transitions from a front facelock (such as suplexes and DDTs).
- Dropping objects from a crouching state no longer attempts to hand them over.
- No shivering animation while sleeping.
- Dropped objects can't be handed to opponents during a match.
- Unconscious wrestlers are eventually removed from arenas if they can't walk out themselves.
- Water is bluer and less transparent.
- The jury reacts to the prosecution & defence as well as the verdict.
- Bloodsport style "Ropeless Ring" matches show up more often - especially in the MMA-based Weekend Warriors promotion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/df09fdb8c0a059504ce37a4df052507e7e22bc9d.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Go Away Heat
notes.notes:
- New "Draft" universe option allows Pro users to jumble up the rosters (it goes without saying that you should BACK UP any cherished data before risking undesirable results!).
- Lots of new taunts include: "Cero Miedo", "3 Point Turn", "Samoan Wave", "Throat Finger", "Blow Kiss", "W Sign", "L Sign", "Bicep Kiss", "Shush", "Here Comes The Boom".
- Roaming in cold outdoor weather (including night in winter months) damages your health more rapidly, as indicated by a discoloured health meter and a shivering animation! This can be offset by the heat of fire.
- The command for deliberately starting fires has switched to PICK-UP + ATTACK instead of taunt (think of "striking" a match!).
- You can deliberately set fire to ANY flammable object nearby instead of just the one you were aiming for - including large furniture!
- Upper body tethers can be used to tug an opponent closer to you if they are too far away to grapple! Spamming it can backfire depending on how much stronger your opponent is.
- Lying grapples are more likely to continue to the head or legs when holding a direction (or during an adrenaline rush so you can rise up into your finisher!), and only ever trigger an instant hold WITHOUT a direction.
- Holds are more likely to fall apart if the necessary limbs are missing!
- Skateboard impacts risk falling over (especially during entrances!).
- Slightly improved swimming physics.
- Wrestlers don't change their costumes at exactly the same time.
- Prevented a rare issue that may have caused the "Epic" arena video screens to crash.
- More lockers can actually store objects on their shelves.
- Signing to Hollywood during a conversation no longer results in a 0-week contract.
- You are only charged for objects you walk out with if you have enough money.
- Booking expenses can never be more than 50% of the show's revenue.
- Friends spend more time together backstage when roaming.
- Managers/partners follow you from scene to scene when roaming, and other players keep control of the same character wherever possible (i.e. until you exit to the titles).
- Prevented any inconsistencies caused by using the 2nd controller to control the star when roaming.
- Updated mod launcher.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/f1d4d91765a1a00e1981f72f9949723685405ce6.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Off The Rails!
notes.notes:
v1.7.3
- Real-time costume changes make it optional to change into your ring gear before your entrance or during it!
- Barriers/railings are destructible at the smaller corners!
- New ring canvases full of sponsors.
- Characters are highlighted by outlines during match setup or when changing controls.
- Missing limbs are not restored every time you start a new career.
- Missing limbs reduce a character's weight.
- Leaving the scene with an "Adrenaline" rush removes the overhead label.
- Unconscious wrestlers are correctly eliminated from all match types (and simulated results).
- Slightly improved collision detection when the head or legs fall near a weapon.
- Right clicks can be used to quickly browse options backwards on PC.
- Middle clicks can be used to instantly reset an option.
- Pro camera options include not being distracted by entrances or eliminations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/ac8d1a6fa7b7b3619d35d6df5fe6abec6f415aff.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Performance Enhancing Drugs
notes.notes:
- New headwear includes a firefighter helmet, wizard/witch hat, and alternative crown/tiara.
- Medical kits and syringes help you restore health/spirit more quickly!
- Consumables are regenerated more reliably.
- Improved collision detection on stomps or ground grapples from taller people.
- Seated grabs don't snatch from other people.
- Improved logic when copying costumes between genders.
- Improved consistency in how severed limbs heal.
- Weight missions are not set if your stats leave no room for improvement.
- Prevented any conflicts between injured dates and court dates.

notes.title: All The Right Moves
notes.notes:
- New family of moves at the front includes various "Alabama" slams and "Dead Head".
- New family of moves at the rear includes various "Wheelbarrow" slams.
- New flying front move includes "Block Buster".
- New "Head Snap" move at the ground.
- Wider variety of handshakes that you can choose in the "Gestures" section (although your choice may not always override the choice of the other person).
- Improved evasion logic prevents glitching out of the ring during a rope turn.
- The controller button you use to unpause is disregarded in the game itself.
- Wrestlers who get knocked out do not automatically have falls scored over them (thereby instantly ending the match) and must still be pinned or found to be unconscious by the referee.

notes.title: Ring Rust
notes.notes:
- Lots of new costumes from the prison game (Hard Time III) include robotic metals!
- New "Transparent 4" hairstyle works as a toupee (which can be applied automatically if you press "Restore Default" on the Wally Stacks character).
- Improved consistency in the colouring of transparent hair length and fringes.
- Age-appropriate relationships with the opposite sex are assumed to be romantic and may include kissing! There is not yet a separate relationship slot for it.
- New taunts include "Goosebumps" and the "Milk America Great Again" dance!
- The motorcycle from Old School is available as the fastest vehicle in wrestling!
- Court case attendance times are highlighted brown when roaming.
- Roaming dialogue is less likely to be delivered in a violent situation.
- The roaming tutorial is only repeated at the default difficulty level or lower.
- Louder thud when landing from a height.
- You don't automatically sleep on a bed if you're angry/hyperactive or pressing any other command.
- Changing weight mission is half as likely.
- Court cases are rarer and fines are lower.
- It's half as likely that team-mates will want to synchronize costumes.
- Severed limbs that are dismissed as a "false alarm" are restored properly.
- There's a rare chance that somebody will die instantly with no writhing!
- Dead/unconscious participants are properly eliminated (including referees).
- Swapping hands while seated no longer risks crashing.
- Changing the venue in exhibitions only resets "Standard" furniture/prop selections, so that unique settings remain intact.
- Adjusted furniture weight to make more of them easier to lift overhead (by holding the command with enough Strength).
- Title match results cannot (yet) be disputed in court.
- Removed console that looked too similar to the N64 because Nintendo can't take a compliment.
- Promotion editor criteria reduced to winning ANY title at each promotion.
- The controller button you use to unpause is disregarded for a split-second in the game itself (i.e. attacking when you didn't intend to).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/d2ba2bee1dd58d2bfec7730bd0972d0bdc2b1f6f.jpg[/img]

notes.title: v1.6.9+
notes.notes: A tiny bit of fine-tuning to the most recent patch ensures that the correct dialogue is always used for the new weight change missions, etc. And you can now "roam" into court the same way you would any other confrontation!

notes.title: Justice Is Served
notes.notes:
- New missions in career mode include gaining/losing weight.
- Hardcore violence is better tolerated in match ratings, and losing limbs gets a bigger pop!
- Hardcore gimmicks are less likely without a rivalry.
- Asking to join someone's promotion via the approach method now has the correct dialogue.
- Court fines are paid to the correct company in booking mode.
- Court cases can't be booked within a month of each other (unless you're the one pressing charges).
- Computers can be used to reveal data about other characters, and reading out of books or magazines sustains the reading animation.
- You can't sleep while having an adrenaline rush or a nervous breakdown.
- You're not blamed for fatalities in career mode unless they were your opponent.
- You're less likely to be taken to court for "interfering" if you were a manager or referee.
- Employees are less likely to complain that they've been "devalued".
- Arena damages are more expensive in career mode (relative to how much you're worth).

notes.title: Court Appeal
notes.notes:
This emergency patch fixes a handful of inconsistencies with the new court cases and gore:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/eb75142929662c1038d4dedd86da94c865c8d336.jpg[/img]

- Lots of new headwear includes earrings, hairbands, and berets.
- New body materials include a zipped up leather jacket (in both black and white).
- Severed limbs are disabled by default unless you go looking for the option.
- You can request to restore a missing limb in the hospital, and bookers can also encourage you to do it like any other surgery.
- The chances of dying from severed limbs are much less.
- Headless characters are treated as eliminations.
- Deceased characters no longer appear as jurors.
- Court cases versus dead opponents are cancelled (and a relevant mourner is more likely to be assigned on their behalf in the first place). In the unlikely event a dead person is involved, the court case (or any other cut-scene) will still be heard to a conclusion.
- Most court cases aren't so common, and certainly don't happen twice in the same month.
- Court fines aren't so high, and can certainly never be more than you own!
- Non-existent news report 819 is now correctly identified as a corrupt booker's attempt to terminate your contract through the courts.
- The promotion editor criteria has changed to winning every World title (or topping the TV charts with each promotion).
- Using a "Splash" as a standing attack no longer confuses the striking system.

notes.title: Hard Times
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/98c73e7fc8313d918ffd8fce80659495b9815bf9.jpg[/img]

- To celebrate the release of the new "Hard Time III" game, grievances can now be heard in court in both career modes! This new location is also accessible in roaming via the black door to the east of the barber shop.
- Handcuffs can be used to temporarily tie an opponent's arms behind their back when you grab them! There is a new gimmick match to this effect.
- The level of gore can be raised to risk losing limbs in particularly dangerous spots! (But this is still realistically rare)
- Shovels can be used to dig tunnels to another location in roaming mode if you step into a large enough hole!
- New objects from the "Old School" game include lots of sports equipment and a backpack for storing a 3rd item!
- Books and a different magazine cover.
- Lots of new food types and more noticeable body changes from your diet & exercise.
- Some locations may now have a computer desk that you can interact with by taunting nearby.
- By holding the pick-up command, furniture can be lifted & thrown overhead by characters who are strong enough!
- A hairdryer lets you access costume editing anywhere when roaming instead of just in the barber shop.
- The gym now has a basketball hoop, where scoring improves your stats!
- Lots of new themes include extracts from the main medley as well as other games.
- Fixed move animations at "Smooth" speed (60fps).
- New responses to assault compare the weapons involved.
- Only aim low at furniture if you're close enough to it.
- Improved AI doesn't interrupt team-mates or enemy eliminations.
- Changing your character's face when setting up a new career is no longer treated as plastic surgery.
- Scars remain visible in backstage meetings.
- Improved logic in Hall Of Fame entries.
- Seated pick-ups no longer smash fragile objects.
- In roaming mode, you only greet allies you have chosen to look at instead of being constantly distracted against your will.
- Either thumbstick button can be used to reset an option instead of both of them.
- Washing in a sink cleans all limbs instead of just the hands.
- Adrenaline rushes boost your health in roaming mode as much as in a match.
- Stat changes are displayed longer under the health meter.
- Pen & paper dialogue sound FX consistent with more recent games. 
- Built in the latest version of Unity for enhanced compatibility.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3009850/Hard_Time_III/

notes.title: Armed & Dangerous
notes.notes:
A new family of arm manipulation moves stretches your opponents to the limit - including a "Vertebreaker", "Crucifix Drop" (Killswitch), and "Pump Handle Slam"! Unfortunately, each one took so long to animate that there wasn't time for much more in this update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/64a30894781ed4a3779d5ef0d3242a94378f654f.jpg[/img]

Elsewhere, new costume possibilities include leg tattoos (that are perfectly placed to be hidden behind boots when you realize you've committed the best years of your career to a struggling brand). New headwear also includes winter hats and variations of existing accessories such as wearing headphones around the neck or shades on your forehead. Also look out for a handful of new props such as toilet tissue, luggage, and rocks/bricks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/652e36950272bf8e4804db60b98499e490a64e6f.jpg[/img]

I also took this opportunity to fix an oversight where it suddenly became impossible to whip people into the barriers. That and other fixes are listed in more detail here:
http://www.mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Trading Blows
notes.notes:
v1.6.5 brings the school game's new headwear to wrestling - including a neck brace! Samoan characters can also now enjoy a wider range of tattoo combinations. Meanwhile, the gameplay under the surface continues to evolve with different ways to "trade blows" organically in a brawl - including the "Samoan Spike" as a dedicated move.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/5a47a62978029dd4ae321f013cfec2d9414b434e.jpg[/img]

To keep things topical, a new camera option also allows you to drain the colour from the screen to look like CCTV footage! Combined with that particular camera angle, it's so effective that it even appears as a legitimate match type in careers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/97abac23c1e059f53fc9ccc70e7e57eda35c2a77.jpg[/img]

All this plus the usual influx of welcome bug fixes and balancing:
http://www.mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: v1-6-4
notes.notes:
Emergency patch to fix an oversight that caused the camera to crash in empty scenes (i.e. no referee at the start of a match). The "Manual" camera is also now an official setting that ensures it never moves unless you want it to.

This patch also offers early access to a new mechanic I'm working on, where more actions can be performed while seated - such as picking up, dropping, and even crafting!

notes.title: Front Row Seat
notes.notes:
Not only is there a new TV studio where interviews can take place, but improved camera controls give you an even better view! With a simple mouse click in the centre of the screen (or a tap of the D-Pad on a controller), you can now temporarily override the angle. A brand new "Spectator" angle also lets you enjoy the action from a static point, while an improved "Square" angle now squares up to the closest of 4 possible sides for improved playability at ANY location. Combined with the manual controls, this means you can effortlessly switch between a 2K style side view or the classic AKI ramp view.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/bd7e5952a163753b003631ce6003c1695409f1ce.jpg[/img]

All this plus the usual intake of bug fixes to keep things stable:
www.mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Happy New Year!
notes.notes:
To celebrate the game's 4th year, a generous amount of new content has arrived! Big shows now take place in a larger new "Epic Arena", which features a ramp & stage with video screens. What takes place in that arena also now includes a handful of stipulations that have never been seen in a wrestling game before - from ropes & chains to water! Less dramatic changes include forbidding strikes or grapples if you want an unusual challenge. All of these are explained in new promos whenever they occur in career mode.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/051618722136ac639ceab1e63ec8e66ee77ae3be.jpg[/img]

Modders should also be aware that the launcher has evolved to give you greater control over the growing amount of content. It assumes you have the .NET6 runtime, so you may want to grab that from Microsoft if you're running an older version of Windows.

notes.title: 64-bit Fix
notes.notes: This version is rebuilt for 64-bit as intended instead of 32-bit, which should reinstate mod support and prevent any other compatibility issues.

notes.title: Everybody Talks Too Much
notes.notes:
Inspired by recent changes in the school game, the multiple choice dialogue system gives you even more to talk about in wrestling! By gesturing towards somebody, you can now initiate a conversation where you press either side to change the subject. Just bear in mind that rejection is as dispiriting as you'd expect to prevent spamming.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/74d7868964734ff6ac3ea4dfb201d3c2350bfb84.jpg[/img]

The v1.6.1 update also features a handful of new hybrid moves - such as the "Powerbomb Powerslam" that enjoyed going viral when it showed up in AEW! LA Knight's "BFT" also appears here known as the "Nightmare". There's also a handful of new costume variations for wearing shirts differently. All this plus the usual intake of fixes and balancing:
http://www.mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Exposed Wood & Stretchers!
notes.notes:
- New "Stretcher" alternative to the standard bed, which can be found in the hospital and sometimes appears at ringside instead of the ladder.
- Canvas options now include exposed wood or metal - which sounds different and scores bonus damage! These also now appear as gimmick matches in career mode.
- New shark mask and reverse headband.
- More feminine sitting poses.
- Reinstated the [Tab] key as a way of sleeping or changing characters on PC.
- Clicking a health meter to switch characters only works in matches.
- Undiscovered characters cannot be called out via the "Interference" option.
- Team names are shown in your calendar profile.
- Changing your face in-game results in temporary scarring to imply cosmetic surgery!
- Wearable objects are removed properly when handed over to somebody else.
- Refusing to buy or sell objects isn't always a negative interaction.
- Light from flickering flames is applied properly in all environments, and no longer lingers as a strong yellow colour.
- Weather & fire FX are affected by the volume setting.
- Reducing the sound volume no longer makes crowd sounds disproportionately quiet.
- Prevented an issue that may have caused managers to warp onto furniture upon making their entrance.
- Roaming into the press room now reveals a row of chairs at the back.
- Slight changes to the default rosters and title belts.

notes.title: Welcome To The Workshop!
notes.notes:
While we all wish it was easier to edit the assets in my new games, Steam Workshop is finally here to at least make it indirectly possible! You can now "subscribe" to a whole range of mods and have them automatically show up in your game by choosing the alternate "Play Modded" launch option: 
https://steamcommunity.com/app/1620340/workshop/


Not only is this easier for users, but it's also fairer for the developer if all of this happens within Steam - where paying customers have earnt the right to customize a game they supported to this point. Once you get comfortable with it, you may even find yourself uploading your own mods! Look out for a couple of new PDFs explaining each side of the process. If enough people support the content, it could become a mutually beneficial way of breathing new life into the game for years to come. May I take this opportunity to publicly thank IngoH for his tireless efforts in taking us this far.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/4f17c199107d93f56622666fd7db22cde09810cd.jpg[/img]

If you know this is never going to be your thing, you can revert back to always launching the vanilla version with a quick tick of that box. This is by no means my way of giving up on the project, as I have plenty of official developments in the pipeline as well.

notes.title: Summer Fashions
notes.notes:
This summer's v1.5.9 update introduces a handful of new costumes to help you recreate certain looks! I also took the opportunity to finally fix the glitchy "Transparent" hair. Other polishing includes a new stumbling alternative to flying off the edge of furniture, which keeps you on your feet more often. The way focusing works in roaming is also evolving, as you now automatically disengage from anybody you repeatedly walk away from. It's still possible to achieve this manually by holding the focus command, which frees up the left stick button for sleeping.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/a7417bbc83b235866f4903553a37d27af1c100bf.jpg[/img]

You can study all the other bug fixes too tiny to mention at the back of the manual:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Street Fighter Combos
notes.notes:
v1.5.8 introduces a handful of classic moves to celebrate the return of Street Fighter! It has been a fun experiment in animating unorthodox attacks with unique mechanics. They're not distributed among the characters as standard, so purists needn't fear as you'll never see them unless you go looking for them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/44cf49de0584852fb621126534cff186fa04a99a.jpg[/img]

This is also the long-awaited update that finally allows personalized team names under the "Relationships" tab, as well as a handful of the usual bug fixes:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Why Did The Chicken Cross The Rhodes?
notes.notes:
You never know what each update could contain when you're trying to keep a wrestling game topical! After taking a month off to see how Wrestlemania panned out, I found myself creating a rubber chicken. I also finally got around to adding my version of the "Cross Rhodes" - which was every bit as hard to animate as I feared, but benefits from being used as a running/flying move from the rear for some wild spots. Inspired by Vikingo's antics on Dynamite, I've also made it possible for especially agile wrestlers to perform SOMERSAULT grapples! You can study the full patch notes here:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/dc470a28c05aae1a631216e62deba0f8a26d5e93.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Mid-Air Collisions
notes.notes:
Inspired by last month's Royal Rumble spot, mid-air collisions are now a spectacle in this game! Whenever 2 flying attacks meet in mid-air, BOTH participants can hit each other and tumble to the ground in a variety of ways. This is, of course, quite rare unless you get performative in multiplayer mode! You're more likely to see it at ground level, where 2 running attacks can also result in a double clothesline.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/80482b743042a34cea480c5160af93c1376b9804.jpg[/img]

Flying or jumping opponents are also now vulnerable to any attack powerful enough to knock them out of the air! We're seeing a steady flow of new such attacks. Inspired by the re-release of Weekend Warriors, its "Spinning Back Kick" and "Spinning Back Elbow" have made a welcome return to this game - as well as a "Shove", which makes its 3D debut after being one of my favourites in 2D.

v1.5.5 also features a handful of new animations elsewhere, and alternative referee voices courtesy of Ross Foad:
http://www.mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Sign Of The Times
notes.notes:
Fresh out of the Christmas break, the project is entering its 3rd year of free updates! The big news is that being able to write text in 3D is changing the way the world communicates with you, as a poster backstage indicates who is in the ring should you choose to interfere. The train also now indicates 8 different destinations through each of its doors. Another nice detail is that the new weather FX are now visible through the windows of indoor locations!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/37dd54963529dfcc9df4daf66a17ce5723377c3a.jpg[/img]

Having lost several people in real life since the last update, v1.5.4 also includes the "Split Kick" from IK+ in memory of Archer Maclean - as well as Jay Briscoe's "Jay Driller" underhook piledriver. Being able to keep things topical is one of the many great privileges of having this much creative freedom!

I've spent much of January fine-tuning how controllers are used in my games, so those users may be interested to take advantage of the new "Calibration" option (via "Cast>Controllers" or the C key from the titles). I did my best to accommodate Xbox & Playstation as standard, but it's good to know you can now adapt to anything else as well.

notes.title: It's beginning to look a lot like Christmas...
notes.notes:
It's beginning to look a lot like Christmas, as seasonal weather such as rain & snow is forecast in my games for the first time! There are also gifts large & small that you can actually open to reveal secret weapons, and the last event of each year now has fun with these festive gimmicks. To celebrate the World Cup at the same time, you may even see a few balls lying around with their own unique physics...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/16010631254c1d42cdafa649612f29207bab0fad.jpg[/img]

Speaking of physics, if you double-tap to either side with an agile wrestler you can now show off a graceful new cartwheel animation! You can even hone this skill in the gym by doing it over the blue mats to score a stat increase. v1.5.3 also fixes its fair share of bugs that were caused by too many particle FX or spawned objects. Hopefully, the chaos is more foolproof now:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Tacked On
notes.notes:
My games were arguably the first to ever use thumbtacks as a weapon (in both 2D & 3D), so now they're back and badder than ever before! An improved higher-resolution effect finally separates each puddle of tacks from the bag itself, allowing you to create your own trails wherever it's dropped. Even broken furniture can now shed a few nails too! Improved collision detection then punishes each individual limb that touches them - including holds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/a2918e3cb3028d4a939774daf4257bc3d81fc451.jpg[/img]

This update also makes the game playable at 60fps via a new "Smooth" camera setting beyond 200% speed. I have mixed feelings about it, as I accomplished a lot at lower frame rates and would hate for this to became the "new normal". It also has a floaty quality that exposes some of the animation instead of making it "better" in my opinion. It never hurts to have options, though, so it's there for you to make your own mind up.

v1.5.2 also includes a fistful of niggling bug fixes that you can study here in further detail:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: In Your Head
notes.notes:
You won't believe your eyes when you see the spooky v1.5.1 update through the new "First Person" camera! Although it's obviously a novelty, it's surprisingly playable and makes roaming even more immersive than it was already. Fighting is every bit as disorientating as it would be in real life, however - and even more likely to leave you with a headache!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/5e026bb41392cb9f1ff4978678b7a49ae7bdc61b.jpg[/img]

This creepy Halloween update also introduces a shovel as a weapon with a unique ability to deface the scenery - and the rare possibility of intruders bursting through the floor! On the other hand, the broom can now be used to literally clean up any mess, and fully interactive reading material now lets you in on the secret:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

Lots of niggling glitches have also been fixed to offer the most stable experience yet.

notes.title: Press Start
notes.notes:
Keeping things topical after recent events, press conferences are now part of YOUR life as a wrestler too! It's a whole new location branching off the backstage area, where you can go during the hour before any high profile 1-on-1 match to put things into context. It's also accessible in exhibitions & booking if your prefer, via a whole other "Broadcasting" promo category.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/795b191d68369f093126d51f88b2a2e4907a505c.jpg[/img]

v1.5.0 also includes a healthy dose of bug fixes. Turning heads no longer get stuck in the wrong direction, and I'm doing my best to reduce clipping and other unsatisfactory interactions with scenery. As my first update as a Steam Deck owner, this is also the one that fine-tunes everything for the handheld - ensuring early adopters have everything running smoothly from now on...

notes.title: Hands On Deck
notes.notes:
I've been blindly developing for the Steam Deck all year, so I'm relieved to see it working so well out of the box with my own eyes! Anything that needs fine-tuning can now happen under my watch, ensuring that PC gaming remains part of my portable revolution. As with the Switch, I set aside a lot of time - and endured a lot of abuse - to keep my games light enough to ride this wave. By the time this tech becomes commonplace, I hope to have a whole series of games that are getting the best out of it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/b4e92c3730827f8bae4ac51510d0abfbd44eb812.jpg[/img]

So far I've only encountered 2 issues:

1) It's a good job the speed option went live in v1.4.9 because it turns out the Steam Deck NEEDS to run at a speed between 101-200%! The animation chokes at 100%, but changing it to so much as 101% knocks it into shape. Now that I know, this will be easy to fix in the next update. 

2) Synching with your desktop via the cloud currently inherits some non-existent controller preferences instead of prioritizing the Deck itself. Again this is easy to fix now I've seen it, but in the meantime simply head to the Options > Cast > Controllers option to confirm you're playing on a handheld.

notes.title: Speed Freaks
notes.notes:
In a feature currently unique to PC users, the speed can now be set precisely between 100% and 200%. Depending on how agreeable your spec is, you may experience some choppier animation or tearing at speeds other than the default - but you at least have the opportunity to see for yourselves. If you get on with it, this preference is also now automatically restored for every other playable scene - allowing you to breeze through the roaming segments as you please!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/b66287caf3ff626ee437ab4b06bedd4a0801dab9.jpg[/img]

This update also makes working for Hollywood slightly more relevant, as you'll find most of those fights now happen at "Backstage" locations like a movie shoot! You can also now choose to start at Hollywood without being moved to a competitive roster.

As ever, all manner of other bug fixes & balancing also help to stabilize your experience:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Wrong Side Of The Tracks
notes.notes:
I've been working to make every location as interesting a wrestling arena, and the subway in the latest example - as it now lets you fall onto the tracks to be hit by a train! You can also wander further down the sides of each platform and up the stairs. Let me know if the extra dimension causes any inconsistencies, but I'm satisfied I've caught most of them. Back in the arena, the work I've been doing even extends to being able to step from one section of the railings to the other.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/997b6c04517c09afd784b0fc7da21c14437d7d80.jpg[/img]

There's also a new "Swing" move to have fun with at the legs, which lets you spin for as long as your strength allows before pressing any button to release. A folding chair is also available as a piece of furniture as well as the classic handheld weapon. There's also a healthy dose of the usual bug fixes to refine your experience:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Title Chase
notes.notes:
June's v1.4.7 update fixes a fistful of niggling bugs, whilst also introducing its fair share of new content - including our first taste of vehicles, as wheelchairs & crutches give more mobility to injured characters! Modders may be interested to know that the game also now reads any correctly named additions to the belt sprites/textures to bring more variety to those. Dozens of (low quality) themes from older games have also been added with one eye on replacing them if you weren't already nostalgic for them!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/9e9b1553c26fb010f0d1c40d101cca3e3913c5c4.jpg[/img]

As ever, the fine print can be found towards the end of the manual:
http://www.mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Crowd Work
notes.notes:
v1.4.6 introduces alternate metal railings, and the crowd behind them even sounds different thanks to a wider variety of FX! New phone gestures even make it possible to take "selfies" with them if you want a cheap pop.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/a81f37c629324bb9918996e901e675bdfdaf058e.jpg[/img]

Under the hood, the most significant change is that training gains are easier to keep. I had tried to discourage becoming superhuman through training, but at least it's less exhausting this way. You should find that weight changes are also more pronounced if you literally want to see more muscle from your strength training!

The other bug fixes too small to mention can be digested here:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Plane Ride From Hell!
notes.notes:
An airport & plane become the latest locations on the map, along with a little fine-tuning to existing ones. It's not as if there's anywhere to fly to yet, but you can at least enjoy recreating the "plane ride from hell" in exhibitions!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/4cf7a22138f04e5358dfccd12989afaff91b3a45.jpg[/img]

There's also more food to eat, as fruit offers a healthier (albeit less satisfying) alternative to junk food. And if you've ever felt there isn't enough time to roam before a show, the clock now pauses on conversations to avoid wasting any. There's not yet enough to do for roaming to become 100% immersive.

notes.title: Ready Player Two
notes.notes: If you've ever tried to enjoy multiplayer only to find that P2 cannot use their left trigger to switch characters, you should find this is fixed in a tiny addition to yesterday's v1.4.2 patch. A handful of other issues too small to mention have also been smoothed over.

notes.title: Food Fight!
notes.notes:
Thanks to some of the more constructive feedback from the 1st week of roaming, there's already plenty that has been refined in v1.4.2:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

As the wrestlers haven't eaten all week, there's also now food as well as drink - with weight changes that are reported in real-time! It's only junk food so far, so your long-term health will suffer if you rely on it for an energy boost.

In memory of Scott Hall, this week's update also sees dozens of new taunts and the "Fallaway Slam" move - along with a cheeky remark from his alter ego...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/9e20b0f60d687bdfd953021291f4201de5b28b14.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Let's Take It Outside!
notes.notes:
Wrestling may have a new heavyweight champion, but I won't drop the lightweight title without a fight! Available now as a free upgrade, v1.4.1 introduces a whole other "roaming" mode that challenges you to take responsibility for what happens behind the scenes in real-time. Seamlessly woven into (and out of) existing careers, you now have as much (or as little) control over your life as you choose to have. Please consult pages 10-11 of the expanded guide for a better understanding of how it works: 
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/35b0537920ef093651e56c56cead0bdd980f786c.jpg[/img]

Coming after just 3 months of focused development, i's only about 50% of what I envisioned for the concept - but there's just enough here to see if it has the potential to go further. I felt compelled to put something in the hands of anybody who feels left out of the next generation of wrestling games. Let's take it outside!

notes.title: Pause For Thought
notes.notes:
Nothing too exciting coming just 1 week after the last update, but some important bug fixes bring stability. If you've ever noticed the Pause menu overheating your computer at an uncapped frame rate, that pesky oversight has finally been fixed once and for all! A couple of issues with health meters and cloning have also been ironed out.
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Chance Of Cloud
notes.notes:
v1.3.8 accidentally went live while I was testing it yesterday, so if you grabbed the version where the new "Cloning" tab doesn't actually work then be sure to upgrade to the v1.3.9 fix!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/32bfb5a138dabc304c7456ddd0e89124e2f4b213.jpg[/img]

That's not the only cloud hanging over it, however, as this version also now backs up your save data to the cloud if you want a consistent experience across multiple devices! It's primarily intended for Steam Deck, of course, so consider opting out via your Steam settings if it's an unwelcome complication.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/5491802525757fd3f7d0aeefc68af8d8609a07c4.jpg[/img]

Not many of the promised new locations are ready to go public yet, but the gym is and now provides an alternate backdrop for matches as well as meetings and editing. Don't forget that the arena balcony can also now be climbed for the first time since 2008! And new weapons include a guitar and tennis racket.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/20ad479bfdc5bd6f0f091a8d5c08805020406d18.jpg[/img]

You can find the small print on every other little tweak here:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: All Hands On Deck
notes.notes:
As a Switch port, Wrestling Empire has a good opportunity to hit the ground running on the Steam Deck! I've yet to get my hands on the hardware myself, but I'm already doing everything on my end to blindly prepare for the handheld. We can no longer assume that everyone is using a physical keyboard, so entering names with a controller now triggers the game's own virtual keyboard. This is also optional under the "Cast > Controllers" tab if you need to change it back, as implying there's no keyboard will also remove it as a control method for the matches themselves. Even keyboard name entry has improved a little, as it clearly highlights what you're changing instead of leaving you guessing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/f94a5d56f210926a7ee5b93c5e83d2857c794b01.jpg[/img]

Ahead of next weekend, this v1.3.7 update also introduces yet another twist to the ONLY wrestling that can legitimately handle a 30-man Royal Rumble! Getting tossed over the ropes now has a 50% chance of scrambling back in, which makes things 100% more interesting. The same process is also used to smash into the office window, as panes of glass join the growing array of weapons:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Interfere with v1.3.5
notes.notes:
v1.3.5 brings a month's worth of polishing that I wasn't able to release over Christmas - the highlight of which is the ability to request specific interferences in exhibitions or booking! Recent additions like leapfrogs and blocking have also found their proper place over time and no longer occur so often. Be sure to study the fine print for every other little tweak:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/031f17fa421ce5dda48a865772424c07fc20314e.jpg[/img]

Those expecting me to rush out roaming will continue to be disappointed for a while yet, as that aspect of the game is nowhere close to being ready and will require my complete concentration going forward - so updates are expected to settle down to once per month. But thanks for supporting the project thus far, as there wouldn't even be a 2022 to look forward to if the press had the last word!

notes.title: Steam Awards Nomination
notes.notes:
Wrestling Empire has already had a good debut on Steam regardless of what happens next, but if those positive reviews translate into positive votes then it could see out the year with a Steam Award! After dozens of free updates that redefined what people expect from a wrestling game, the "Labor Of Love" championship sounds like the one worth fighting for. Wrestling games are automatically disqualified from awards if the judges don't happen to be fans, so we mustn't waste this opportunity to represent the genre.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/4fe28a3dd85c589dea9fc580a141355428568768.png[/img]

notes.title: Leapfrog to v1.3.4
notes.notes:
Leapfrog to v1.3.4 with more evasive manoeuvres for agile wrestlers, as well as a fistful of improvements to the AI and collision detection. I finally fixed an issue that was preventing strikes from connecting. The focusing system has also been modified, as I found it was too hard to turn your attention to outside parties. Now you tap the command once with a direction to find the nearest opponent or press it repeatedly to browse through ALL viable targets.  Hold to disengage completely.
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Promotion Editor
notes.notes:
Just when you think you've seen it all, you can now change what you're seeing! Upon taking each promotion to the top of the ratings (which is now signified by a golden pen) or winning every title at every promotion, you can unlock special editing privileges for the brand as well as its roster. It's mostly useful for changing the names and colours of each championship belt. Although there’s no easy way to change the logo along with the brand name, this at least meets the modders halfway. You can even change the colour associated with each brand, which now subtly changes the background colour itself as well as the territory. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40576076/617ab1bec374d5b44cb6de553cb1149a0a9385e0.jpg[/img]

This update also takes another pass at balancing the books, as I found it was too easy to coast through the booking mode with a popular champion. Their popularity now only accounts for a THIRD of the house instead of half, putting more focus on a good in-ring product to achieve the final number. Meanwhile, rival territories are also more competitive to keep you on your toes! As ever, there's also a handful of new moves to look out for:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: v1.3.1
notes.notes:
New features can occur too often at first before finding their place, which is the kind of balance that v1.3.1 brings. It also introduces a handful of other game changers - such as stumbling instead of falling and hurting either hand from spamming strikes!
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: New Weapons Coming In Hot!
notes.notes: v1.3.0 introduces lot of new weapons - and makes setting fire to them a deliberate choice by pressing Taunt and Pick-Up at the same time! Some related balancing issues also help to tidy up the action.

notes.title: v1.2.9
notes.notes:
New pins and holds offer another evolutionary step forward for the in-ring product! Lots of alternative animations filter down to every aspect of the game - including a condensed kneeling state to stop referees leaning in too close.
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: v1.2.8
notes.notes:
A belated v1.2.8 update brings the best of both worlds - with consumable beverages and smashed glass for hardcore fans, as well as a plethora of new holds and MMA transitions for grappling purists! There's also all the usual fine-tuning, which most notably gives attendances an upper limit closer to 10k - and more taxation on wealthy companies to keep the pressure as high as your income. I've also closed a loophole that made your booker an inordinately entertaining guest referee.
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: All Out War
notes.notes: v1.2.6 brings a little bit of everything in one of the most substantial updates yet! Invading rival territories now risks triggering a very real inter-promotional war - from backstage brawls to in-ring competition. Ahead of Darby Allin's match against CM Punk this weekend, you can also have fun with his "Coffin Drop" and skateboard (both at the same time if you get creative with it!). Plus all the usual bug fixes that keep every release that little bit more stable.

notes.title: 50 Characters Or Less
notes.notes:
As of the latest update, higher end PCs are now free to expand to the cast limit to 50 characters in the ring at the same time! That was always indirectly possible via the "Surprise Intervals" match format, but now it's officially possible before your eyes. I could push it even further, but it's the concept of wrestling itself that could not cope with more! That's something to look forward to if other free-roaming adventures come to the platform, which is looking more likely if this game's "Very Positive" first month can be sustained.

This update also contains a handful of other developments that can be better digested towards the end of the manual:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: New Faces
notes.notes: In a rush to populate the rosters, early versions of the game borrowed too heavily from famous faces - which is a bad habit I'll have to wean myself off to grow beyond this level. The new ones aren't "supposed to" look like anybody in particular, but they do benefit from being redrawn at a higher resolution. I also learnt some new Photoshop skills along the way, which bodes well for the future!

notes.title: v1.2.4
notes.notes: Booking made the world a lot more complicated and shot some holes in the schedule of the original career mode! Please upgrade to v1.2.4 for a more stable experience across both modes. As the manual explains, they are supposed to run parallel in a "shared universe" to preserve rosters and title histories - so consider playing one mode at a time if any disruptions are unwelcome.

notes.title: Fully Booked
notes.notes:
The booking mode that puts the "empire" in Wrestling Empire is now available at no extra cost! Thanks to everybody who supported the project to bring it to fruition ahead of schedule after 6 weeks of focused work. It's still early days for the concept and it's being refined all the time, but there's plenty here to keep you busy over the summer. Don't forget to study the updated manual, which now includes some helpful booking tips in the middle:
http://mdickie.com/guides/wempire.pdf

notes.title: Frame Rate Fix
notes.notes: Early adopters this morning may have experienced unwieldly frame rates on display frequencies above 60Hz, which has hopefully now been fixed in an urgent v1.2.0 update.

notes.title: Demo Link
notes.notes:
I did submit a demo to Steam at the same time, but it appears to be inaccessible. You can grab it directly from the Windows icon of my own website:
http://mdickie.com/games_unity.htm

It is strongly recommended that you do so before buying the full game, as I'm hearing that it does not run at the intended speed on all specs. I am not yet able to replicate the issue on any PC I own, but I hope a universal solution will present itself as soon as possible.
